literal: One's own wealth, they say, one's own children; their wealth by their respective deeds will come.
translation: It is said that one's own children are one's true wealth, and that this wealth comes to a person through their own respective deeds.
modern: தம் மக்கள் தான் தம்முடைய உண்மையான செல்வம் என்று கூறுவர்; அந்தச் செல்வமானது அவரவர் செய்யும் செயல்களின் வழியாகவே வந்து சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet defines children as the true wealth of a person. The phrase 'they say' indicates an accepted wisdom that material wealth is secondary to one's offspring. The word 'அவர்' (their) in the second line refers to the children, making 'அவர் பொருள்' mean 'the wealth that is them'. The second half explains that this precious wealth is attained as a result of the parents' own respective deeds. Thus, the blessing of having good children is directly linked to one's own actions.
